A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and proposed discretization method. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite the added theory and reorganized appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original results on 18 regression and 15 classification datasets, controlled synthetic experiments, binning runtimes, and supplementary low-bin-budget and XGBoost experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original accuracy and timing measurements for alternative optimal discretizers in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both versions propose quantile-initialized Lloyd k-means for feature discretization before GBDT training. The new population formulation supplies theoretical motivation; optimal discretizers are comparison methods, and streaming k-means is only suggested for future work.

E1.justification: The same 33 OpenML datasets and five synthetic diagnostic scenarios remain. Appendix D reuses Abalone and Diamonds. Neither these additional discretizer comparisons nor the added training-runtime reference introduces a new dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix D/Table 4 adds MILP-optimal regression binning and dynamic-programming optimal 1-D k-means against quantile and Lloyd k-means on two retained datasets. Figure 3 adds an XGBoost training-time reference. The main accuracy comparator sets remain unchanged; Exact is renamed Exhaustive.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D comparison measures per-split preprocessing time, test MSE, and reference training time on a single M1 thread using the existing hyperparameter search space. Figure 3 extends the timing comparison to training. Existing main-experiment splits, bin budgets, tuning procedures, and synthetic generator remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a skewness-estimator sensitivity check, reporting changes below 0.005 between biased and unbiased estimates. Appendix D examines whether globally optimal binning improves the heuristic's speed–accuracy tradeoff. The existing synthetic, low-bin-budget, and XGBoost analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Appendix H, Tables 7–9, supplies standard errors across random states for the retained main, low-bin-budget, and XGBoost results; v1 reported means and significance markers without these uncertainty magnitudes. The stated 20 benchmark splits, 50 synthetic draws, t-tests, and multiple-testing correction remain unchanged, so additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: All 54 retained real-world result rows have unchanged means. v2 adds optimal-binner accuracy/runtime results, dataset skewness values, and a training-runtime curve. Reported 10M-row quantile/k-means times change from 2.5/5.1 to 2.0/5.5 seconds. Regression MRR prose is corrected from 0.75/0.60 to 0.65/0.72 for k-means/quantile, and win-count summaries are corrected to match existing tables.

T1.justification: v1 leaves theoretical characterization to future work. v2 Section 3 introduces population binning definitions, a paired-difference lemma, and a theorem deriving an explained-variance lower bound under Lipschitz, finite-moment, and independent-noise assumptions. Appendix A establishes equality for linear targets.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion add a theoretical optimality/lower-bound result as a central contribution to the previously empirical case. The library-level k-means recommendation remains, while the abstract's significant regression-win count is corrected from four to three.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses for quantile's small low-budget wins: allocating scarce bins to irrelevant extremes and chance alignment of bin edges with labels. It also interprets the optimal-binner tradeoffs, distinguishes population-optimal binning from Lloyd approximation, and discusses unevaluated streaming alternatives. Existing production-integration and target-boundary limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the skewness calculation and supplies hardware and timing details for the new alternative-binner benchmark. Conversely, v1's explicit public repository and Apache 2.0 license statement is replaced by an anonymized reviewer-package reference to a Links section absent from v2, weakening concrete code-access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Arthur and Vassilvitskii, Navas-Palencia, and Sculley for initialization, optimal binning, and streaming clustering. Related work also distinguishes LightGBM's post-binning row sampling from bin construction. The positioning as a systematic comparison of unsupervised GBDT discretizers is retained.

P1.justification: Most empirical prose and its sequence remain. Selected background, related-work, results, efficiency, and generator explanations are expanded or revised, and Exact becomes Exhaustive. References move before the appendices, whose retained material is reorganized alongside the new sections.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different journal layout, adds the alternative-binner table, expands the dataset table with skewness, and redisplays retained results in three standard-error tables. Figure 3 is redrawn with a training-time curve; heatmaps are resized and the all-exponential row clarified. Table significance markers change from asterisks to bold.

improvement.justification: v2 improves statistical transparency and consistency through standard errors and corrected MRR/win summaries; its theory and targeted speed–accuracy checks strengthen the rationale. These gains are qualified: the theorem concerns population-optimal bins rather than guaranteeing the implemented Lloyd heuristic, and the explicit public code/license reference is replaced by an unresolved reviewer-package pointer.
